We need to analyze conceptual meaning of each option (two-part couplet). Determine which one deviates.

We have four options, each appears to be about love (عشق). Let's translate roughly.

Option1: "بیفتد آن که در این راه با شتاب رود - طریق عشق پرآشوب و فتنه است ای دل"
First line: "May he fall who rushes in this path with haste" (or "May the one who goes quickly in this path fall"). Second line: "The way of love is turbulent and full of strife, O heart". So concept: warning about love being tumultuous; haste leads to downfall.

Option2: "باللّه کز آفتاب فلک خوبتر شوی - گر نور عشق حق به دل و جانت اوفتد"
First line: "By God, you become better than the sun of the heavens" (maybe praising). Second line: "If the light of true love falls into your heart and soul". So concept: love as divine light that elevates, making you superior to celestial sun. Positive uplifting.

Option3: "فلک به شعشعه آفتاب شانه کند - شکوه عشق نگه کن که موی مجنون را"
First line: "The heavens (sky) combs with the rays of the sun" maybe meaning the sky is illuminated. Second line: "Guard the glory of love, for (the) hair of Majnun". Not clear. Could be praising love's grandeur; maybe referencing Majnun's love. Likely positive about love's splendor.

Option4: "هر کس که در این بادیه دیوانه عشق است - فرزانه درآید به پری المنزل مقصود"
First line: "Whoever is a lover mad in this desert". Second line: "A wise one will come to the fairy (or beloved) of the intended house". So concept: love as madness in desert, but wise one reaches the goal. Might be about love's journey, perhaps positive.

We need common theme among three and one deviates.

Let's examine: Option1 warns of love's turbulence and haste leads to downfall (negative). Options2,3,4 seem to praise love, talk about its light, glory, wise attainment. So Option1 is the outlier (negative). However Option4 includes "madness" but also "wise will reach the fairy". Could be also about love as a journey but not necessarily negative. Option3 seems a bit obscure but likely praising love's splendor.

Thus answer likely 1.

Check if any other nuance: Option2 includes "by God you become better than the sun of heavens" - that's praising love's effect. Option3: "Heavens comb with sun's rays - guard the splendor of love that (something)". Probably praising love's grandeur. Option4: "Anyone who is a mad lover in this desert - wise will come to the fairy of the house of purpose". Could be about love as madness but wise leads to goal. That's still positive about love's ultimate reward. So yes Option1 is different.

Thus final answer: 1.
